history.caption: Three states' residency tests become three mechanical day counters — short, medium, and fully extended — set at different latching points on a desk.
history.title: Three state residency counters as mechanical tally gates

style_when: the story is a single number, rule, gate or shift and restraint is the point — with no scene to photograph, the frame must still be a real assembly: a modular bay, an unlatched inspection gate, a rack of blades, an interlocking connector
prompt: Three modular mechanical day counters sit on a matte oak home-office desk, arranged in a row at the left third; the first has a short brass tally slat barely extended, the second a mid-length graphite slat, the third a fully extended rust steel slat, each with an unmarked latching gate locked at a different notch. One directional raking light from the left throws long contact shadows across the desk; bone white, graphite, rust palette; brushed steel, brass, oak, paper; extreme asymmetry with generous negative space to the right.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, watermarks, legible numbers
rationale: The article is about statutory thresholds and sequential gates, not a physical facility. Component_assembly makes the three different state counts tangible as modular mechanical counters without literal stock imagery.
subject: three mechanical day counters with different tally slat extensions and latching gates on a desk
core_thesis: Each state publishes its own residency count — California 546 days under employment contract, Oregon 30 days after full abode surrender, Virginia 183 days with an abode — so leaving is a set of dated acts, not a flight.
core_conflict: A state's continued domiciliary claim versus the expat's departure date and abode severance, with numerical thresholds that differ by state.
composition: extreme asymmetry with the counters placed on the left third and a long rightward cast shadow leaving generous negative space
alt_text: Three machined day counters, their brass tally slats pulled out to different lengths, on a pale oak desk.
caption: Three counters, three different day counts: the state's own statute sets the number, not the flight.
title: Move Abroad, Still A Resident After 546 Days

review.depicts: Three rectangular box-like devices — one brushed silver, one matte charcoal, one walnut-brown wood — each with a narrow slot along the top, a small sliding brass latch and a protruding slat at one end, arranged diagonally on a light oak desk lit by strong sun, with long shadows cast to the right and blank white papers plus a shallow brass tray at the lower left.
review.reason: The three similar-but-differently-configured tally devices standing in for the three states and their divergent day counts map onto the article's core mechanism of counting residency days, though without numerals or labels a reader might read them as generic desk objects.
